translation_en: Al-Hasan al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated this to us: Ya'qub, Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, with this chain. He added: When Allah delivered Caesar from the Persian armies, he walked from Hims to Iliya' in gratitude for what Allah had done for him. In the hadith he said: From Muhammad, the servant of Allah and His Messenger. He said: the sin of the Yarisiyyin, and: with the call of Islam.

Yusuf ibn Hammad al-Ma'ni narrated to me: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas: The Prophet of Allah wrote to Kisra, Caesar, the Negus, and every tyrant, calling them to Allah Most High. This was not the Negus over whom the Prophet prayed.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Razzi narrated this to us: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, who narrated to us from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, with the like of it. He did not say that this was not the Negus over whom the Prophet prayed.

Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami narrated this to me: my father informed me: Khalid ibn Qays narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Anas, who did not mention that this was not the Negus over whom the Prophet prayed.

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh informed me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Kathir ibn 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib narrated to me: 'Abbas said: I was with the Messenger of Allah on the day of Hunayn. Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and I stayed close to the Messenger of Allah and did not leave him. The Messenger of Allah was riding a white mule given to him by Farwah ibn Nufathah al-Judhami. When the Muslims and the disbelievers met, the Muslims turned and fled. The Messenger of Allah began driving his mule toward the disbelievers. 'Abbas said: I was holding the bridle of the Messenger of Allah's mule, restraining it so it would not rush forward, while Abu Sufyan held the Messenger of Allah's stirrup. The Messenger of Allah said: 'Abbas, call out to the people of the tree. 'Abbas said: I had a loud voice, so I called at the top of my voice: Where are the people of the tree? By Allah, when they heard my voice, they turned back like cows turning to their calves. They called: Here we are, here we are! Then they fought the disbelievers, and the call among the Ansar was: O Ansar! O Ansar! Then the call was narrowed to Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, and they were called: O Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj! O Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj! The Messenger of Allah looked from atop his mule as if stretching himself toward their battle and said: Now the fighting has become fierce. Then the Messenger of Allah took some pebbles and threw them at the faces of the disbelievers, then said: They are defeated, by the Lord of Muhammad! I went to look, and the fighting still seemed to be as it was. But by Allah, it was only after he threw those pebbles that I continued to see their strength blunted and their cause in retreat.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Muhammad ibn Rafi', and 'Abd ibn Humayd all narrated this to us, from 'Abd al-Razzaq: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, with this chain and the like of it, except that it says Farwah ibn Nu'amah al-Judhami. It says: They are defeated, by the Lord of the Ka'bah! They are defeated, by the Lord of the Ka'bah! It adds: until Allah defeated them. I can almost see the Prophet riding his mule behind them.

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated this to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Kathir ibn al-'Abbas informed me, from his father: I was with the Prophet on the day of Hunayn. He related the hadith. Yunus's and Ma'mar's reports are longer and more complete.

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Abu Khaythamah informed us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: A man asked al-Bara': Abu 'Umarah, did you flee on the day of Hunayn? He said: No, by Allah, the Messenger of Allah did not turn back. Rather, some of his young and lightly equipped Companions went out without armor, or with little armor. They met a people of archers, the combined forces of Hawazin and Banu Nasr, whose arrows almost never missed. They showered them with arrows, and the men retreated toward the Messenger of Allah, who was riding his white mule, led by Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib. He dismounted, sought help, and said: I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib. Then he lined up the people.

Ahmad ibn Janab al-Missisi narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Abu Ishaq, who said: A man came to al-Bara' and asked: Abu 'Umarah, did you turn back on the day of Hunayn? He said: I testify that the Prophet of Allah did not turn back. Rather, some lightly equipped and unarmored people went toward that clan of Hawazin, who were archers. They shot them with a volley of arrows like a swarm of locusts, and the people scattered. They then came toward the Messenger of Allah, with Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith leading his mule. The Prophet dismounted, supplicated, and sought help, saying: I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib. O Allah, send down Your help. Al-Bara' said: By Allah, when the fighting grew fierce, we used him as our shield; the bravest among us was the one who stood beside him, meaning the Prophet.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us. The wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's. They said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara'. A man from Qays asked him: Did you flee from the Messenger of Allah on the day of Hunayn? Al-Bara' said: The Messenger of Allah did not flee. Hawazin were archers that day. When we charged them, they scattered, and we bent over to collect the spoils, but they met us with arrows. I saw the Messenger of Allah on his white mule, with Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith holding its bridle. He was saying: I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib.

Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Abu Bakr ibn Khallad narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: Abu Ishaq narrated to me, from al-Bara'. A man said to him: Abu 'Umarah... He related the hadith, but his report is shorter than theirs, and their report is more complete.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: 'Umar ibn Yunus al-Hanafi narrated to us: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: Iyas ibn Salamah narrated to me: my father said: We went on the Hunayn campaign with the Messenger of Allah. When we faced the enemy, I advanced and climbed a hill. A man from the enemy met me, and I shot an arrow at him. He disappeared from my sight, and I did not know what had happened to him. I looked toward the people and saw them coming over another hill. They met the Prophet's Companions, who turned and fled. I turned back in defeat. I was wearing two cloaks, one as a waist wrap and the other over my shoulders. My waist wrap came loose, so I gathered both garments together as I passed the Messenger of Allah, who was riding a gray mule. He said: Ibn al-Akwa' has seen panic. When the enemy came close to the Messenger of Allah, he dismounted, took a handful of dust from the ground, faced them, and said: May the faces be disfigured! Allah made every one of them have his eyes filled with dust from that handful. They turned and fled, and Allah, Mighty and Exalted, defeated them. The Messenger of Allah divided their spoils among the Muslims.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ibn Numayr all reported from Sufyan. Zuhayr said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Abu al-'Abbas, the blind poet, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah besieged the people of Ta'if but gained nothing from them. He said: We will depart, if Allah wills. His Companions said: We will return without conquering it. The Messenger of Allah said: Go out to fight tomorrow. They went out and suffered wounds. The Messenger of Allah then said: We will depart tomorrow. They were pleased by that, and the Messenger of Allah laughed.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Affan narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas: When news reached the Messenger of Allah that Abu Sufyan was approaching, he consulted the people. Abu Bakr spoke, but the Messenger of Allah turned away from him. Then 'Umar spoke, and he turned away from him. Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah stood and said: Is it us you mean, Messenger of Allah? By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you ordered us to plunge our horses into the sea, we would do so; if you ordered us to drive them to Bark al-Ghimad, we would do it. The Messenger of Allah called the people to set out, and they went until they camped at Badr. Quraysh's water carriers arrived, including a black youth belonging to Banu al-Hajjaj. They seized him, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah asked him about Abu Sufyan and his companions. He said: I know nothing about Abu Sufyan, but here are Abu Jahl, 'Utbah, Shaybah, and Umayyah ibn Khalaf. When he said this, they struck him. He then said: Yes, I will tell you; this is Abu Sufyan. When they left him, they asked again. He said: I know nothing about Abu Sufyan, but Abu Jahl, 'Utbah, and Umayyah ibn Khalaf are among the people. When he said this too, they struck him. The Messenger of Allah was standing in prayer. When he saw this, he turned away and said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, you strike him when he tells you the truth and leave him when he lies. Then the Messenger of Allah said: This is the place where so-and-so will fall. He placed his hand on the ground here and here. None of them moved beyond the place where the Messenger of Allah had put his hand.
